studies.title: Open-String Duet
studies.goal: Play a steady beat on open strings while the teacher plays the tune
studies.spec: E minor, 16 bars, 4/4. Student: only the open strings 6, 5 and 4 (E, A, D) in half and quarter notes: bars 1-4 open E, 5-8 open A, 9-12 open D, 13-16 E A D E. Teacher (or app): Em, Am and D chords and an original melody above, so each open string is the root of the chord. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: First Notes on String 1
studies.goal: E, F and G on the thinnest string
studies.spec: C major, 8 bars, 4/4, quarter and half notes. Notes: the open string 1 (E), string 1 fret 1 (F) with finger 1, string 1 fret 3 (G) with finger 3. Mostly steps, one skip E-G. Teacher part: C and G7, one chord per bar; every melody note must belong to the chord under it or pass by step. End on E over C. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: First Notes on String 2
studies.goal: B, C and D on string 2, then join them to string 1
studies.spec: G major, 8 bars, 4/4. Notes: the open string 2 (B), string 2 fret 1 (C) with finger 1, string 2 fret 3 (D) with finger 3. Bars 5-8 add string 1 (E F G) so the melody crosses between strings 2 and 1. Teacher part: G and C. End on B or D over G. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: First Notes on String 3
studies.goal: G and A on string 3, then a tune across strings 3, 2 and 1
studies.spec: G major, 8 bars, 4/4. Notes: the open string 3 (G) and string 3 fret 2 (A) with finger 2; bars 5-8 use strings 3, 2 and 1 together (G A B C D, and the open string 1 (E)). Teacher part: G and D7 (A sits in D7). End on G. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: First Notes on String 4
studies.goal: D, E and F on string 4
studies.spec: D minor colour, 8 bars, 4/4. Notes: the open string 4 (D), string 4 fret 2 (E) with finger 2, string 4 fret 3 (F) with finger 3. Point out that E to F is a half step (one fret) and D to E a whole step (two frets). Teacher part: Dm and A7. End on D. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: First Notes on String 5
studies.goal: A, B and C on string 5
studies.spec: A minor, 8 bars, 4/4. Notes: the open string 5 (A), string 5 fret 2 (B) with finger 2, string 5 fret 3 (C) with finger 3. Teacher part: Am and E7 (B sits in E7, C and A in Am). End on A. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: First Notes on String 6
studies.goal: E, F and G on the thickest string
studies.spec: E Phrygian colour, 8 bars, 4/4. Notes: the open string 6 (E), string 6 fret 1 (F) with finger 1, string 6 fret 3 (G) with finger 3. Teacher part alternates Em and F: a Spanish-sounding colour that rewards the half step E-F. End on E. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Strumming: Steady Quarters
studies.goal: Four even downstrums per bar, never stopping
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4: Em (022000) for 4 bars, A (x02220) for 4, Em for 4, A for 4. Downstrums on every beat, accent on beat 1. Start at 60 and raise in steps of 4.

studies.title: Change: A and E7
studies.goal: Clean changes: A (x02220) and E7 (020100), the chords of Skip to My Lou
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, strummed. For each pair: 2 bars changing every 2 bars (one strum per bar), 2 bars changing every bar (two strums per bar), 2 bars changing every bar (four strums per bar), 2 bars changing every 2 beats. Metronome on; the change must land on the beat even if the last strum before it is played on open strings. Only one pair, so the 8-bar template runs twice. No finger can stay: lift all fingers together and land them together; E7 needs finger 2 on string 5 fret 2 (B) and finger 1 on string 3 fret 1 (G#), practised as a shape in the air first.

studies.title: Change: Em-D and Em-G
studies.goal: Clean changes: Em (022000) with D (xx0232), then Em with G (320003)
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, strummed. For each pair: 2 bars changing every 2 bars (one strum per bar), 2 bars changing every bar (two strums per bar), 2 bars changing every bar (four strums per bar), 2 bars changing every 2 beats. Metronome on; the change must land on the beat even if the last strum before it is played on open strings. D: finger 1 on string 3 fret 2 (A), finger 3 on string 2 fret 3 (D), finger 2 on string 1 fret 2 (F#); strum strings 4-1 only. Em and G share string 5 fret 2 (B): finger Em with 1 and 2 (1 on string 5, 2 on string 4) and G with 2 on string 6 fret 3 (G), 1 on string 5 fret 2 (B), 3 on string 1 fret 3 (G), and finger 1 never leaves the string.

studies.title: Change: D-A7 and A-D
studies.goal: Clean changes: D (xx0232) with A7 (x02020), then A (x02220) with D
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, strummed. For each pair: 2 bars changing every 2 bars (one strum per bar), 2 bars changing every bar (two strums per bar), 2 bars changing every bar (four strums per bar), 2 bars changing every 2 beats. Metronome on; the change must land on the beat even if the last strum before it is played on open strings. A7 with fingers 2 and 3 on string 4 fret 2 (E) and string 2 fret 2 (C#). A and D share string 3 fret 2 (A): finger A as 2-1-3 (2 on string 4, 1 on string 3, 3 on string 2) and finger 1 stays on string 3 for the D.

studies.title: Change: G-C and C-G7
studies.goal: Clean changes: G (320003) with C (x32010), then C with G7 (320001)
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, strummed. For each pair: 2 bars changing every 2 bars (one strum per bar), 2 bars changing every bar (two strums per bar), 2 bars changing every bar (four strums per bar), 2 bars changing every 2 beats. Metronome on; the change must land on the beat even if the last strum before it is played on open strings. Finger G with fingers 3, 2 and 4 (3 on string 6 fret 3 (G), 2 on string 5 fret 2 (B), 4 on string 1 fret 3 (G)), a second way to finger G, chosen because it makes this change easy: moving to C, fingers 3 and 2 keep their shape and move one string toward string 1 (string 5 fret 3 (C), string 4 fret 2 (E)), and finger 1 lands on string 2 fret 1 (C). C to G7: the same 3-2 shape moves back one string toward string 6, and finger 1 moves from string 2 fret 1 (C) to string 1 fret 1 (F).

studies.title: Change: G-D7 and D-G
studies.goal: Clean changes: G (320003) with D7 (xx0212), then D (xx0232) with G
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, strummed. For each pair: 2 bars changing every 2 bars (one strum per bar), 2 bars changing every bar (two strums per bar), 2 bars changing every bar (four strums per bar), 2 bars changing every 2 beats. Metronome on; the change must land on the beat even if the last strum before it is played on open strings. D7 is a small slanted triangle: 2 on string 3 fret 2 (A), 1 on string 2 fret 1 (C), 3 on string 1 fret 2 (F#); strum strings 4-1. For D-G use the four-finger G (320033): finger 3 on string 2 fret 3 (D) stays put for the D chord, finger 4 takes string 1 fret 3 (G).

studies.title: Change: C-Am and Am-Dm
studies.goal: Clean changes: C (x32010) with Am (x02210), then Am with Dm (xx0231)
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, strummed. For each pair: 2 bars changing every 2 bars (one strum per bar), 2 bars changing every bar (two strums per bar), 2 bars changing every bar (four strums per bar), 2 bars changing every 2 beats. Metronome on; the change must land on the beat even if the last strum before it is played on open strings. C to Am: fingers 1 and 2 stay (string 2 fret 1 (C), string 4 fret 2 (E)); only finger 3 moves, from string 5 fret 3 (C) to string 3 fret 2 (A). Am and Dm share the note on string 3 fret 2 (A), but with different fingers (3 in Am, 2 in Dm): the note stays, the finger changes. Dm: 1 on string 1 fret 1 (F), 3 on string 2 fret 3 (D); strum strings 4-1.

studies.title: Change: Am-E and E-B7
studies.goal: Clean changes: Am (x02210) with E (022100), then E with B7 (x21202)
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, strummed. For each pair: 2 bars changing every 2 bars (one strum per bar), 2 bars changing every bar (two strums per bar), 2 bars changing every bar (four strums per bar), 2 bars changing every 2 beats. Metronome on; the change must land on the beat even if the last strum before it is played on open strings. Am to E is the same shape moved one string toward string 6: Am (2 on string 4, 3 on string 3, 1 on string 2) becomes E (2 on string 5 fret 2 (B), 3 on string 4 fret 2 (E), 1 on string 3 fret 1 (G#)). E to B7: finger 2 stays on string 5 fret 2 (B); B7 adds 1 on string 4 fret 1 (D#), 3 on string 3 fret 2 (A), 4 on string 1 fret 2 (F#), string 2 open; strum strings 5-1.

studies.title: Change: Am-Fmaj7 and C-F
studies.goal: Clean changes: Am (x02210) with Fmaj7 (xx3210), then C (x32010) with the small F (xx3211)
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, strummed. For each pair: 2 bars changing every 2 bars (one strum per bar), 2 bars changing every bar (two strums per bar), 2 bars changing every bar (four strums per bar), 2 bars changing every 2 beats. Metronome on; the change must land on the beat even if the last strum before it is played on open strings. Am to Fmaj7: finger 1 stays on string 2 fret 1 (C); Fmaj7 puts 3 on string 4 fret 3 (F) and 2 on string 3 fret 2 (A). C to F: finger 1 flattens to cover strings 2 and 1 at fret 1 (a two-string barre), the first step toward the full F. Strum strings 4-1 for both F shapes.

studies.title: Change: Em-Am and Em-B7
studies.goal: Clean changes: Em (022000) with Am (x02210), then Em with B7 (x21202): the minor-key changes
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, strummed. For each pair: 2 bars changing every 2 bars (one strum per bar), 2 bars changing every bar (two strums per bar), 2 bars changing every bar (four strums per bar), 2 bars changing every 2 beats. Metronome on; the change must land on the beat even if the last strum before it is played on open strings. Finger Em with 2 and 3: moving to Am, that pair moves one string toward string 1 (to string 4 fret 2 (E) and string 3 fret 2 (A)) and finger 1 adds string 2 fret 1 (C). Em to B7: finger 2 stays on string 5 fret 2 (B).

studies.title: Strumming: Down-Up Eighths
studies.goal: Constant down-up motion with downs on the beat and ups on the and
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, Em (022000) and D (xx0232), 2 bars each. Eighth notes: down on 1 2 3 4, up on every and. Last 8 bars: accent beats 2 and 4.

studies.title: Strumming: Waltz (Bass-Strum-Strum)
studies.goal: Feel 3/4: bass note on 1, strums on 2 and 3
studies.spec: 16 bars, 3/4, D (xx0232) and A7 (x02020), 2 bars each. Beat 1: the bass note alone (open string 4 (D) under D, open string 5 (A) under A7); beats 2 and 3: downstrums on strings 3-1.

studies.title: Strumming: The Folk Pattern
studies.goal: The all-purpose pattern: down, down-up, (miss), up, down-up
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, G (320003), C (x32010), D (xx0232), G: 4 bars each. Pattern per bar: down on 1, down on 2, up on the and of 2, no strum on 3 (the hand still moves down without touching), up on the and of 3, down on 4, up on the and of 4.

studies.title: Strumming: 6/8
studies.goal: Two beats per bar, each in three
studies.spec: 16 bars, 6/8, Em (022000), C (x32010), D (xx0232), Em, 4 bars each. Count 1 2 3 4 5 6: down on 1, down on 2, up on 3, down on 4, down on 5, up on 6; accents on 1 and 4.

studies.title: Strumming: Boom-Chick
studies.goal: Alternate a bass note and a strum, country style
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, G, C, D7, G (4 bars each). Bass note on beats 1 and 3, strum strings 4-1 on 2 and 4. Bass notes: G alternates string 6 fret 3 (G) and the open string 4 (D); C alternates string 5 fret 3 (C) and string 6 fret 3 (G) (finger 3 moves); D7 alternates the open string 4 (D) and the open string 5 (A). Shapes G (320003), C (x32010), D7 (xx0212). In bar 4, walk up into C: bass notes on every beat, string 6 fret 3 (G), the open string 5 (A), string 5 fret 2 (B), then C arrives on string 5 fret 3 (C) on beat 1 of bar 5.

studies.title: Sus Chords and Chord Embellishments
studies.goal: Decorate open chords with sus2, sus4 and add9 notes to keep a strum moving
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, the folk pattern from st-strum-folk. D (xx0232) with Dsus4 (xx0233) and Dsus2 (xx0230); A (x02220) with Asus4 (x02230) and Asus2 (x02200); C (x32010) with Cadd9 (x32030). In each bar: the plain chord on beats 1 and 2, the decorated chord on beat 3 (add or lift one finger, nothing else moves), back to the plain chord on beat 4. Explain the names in plain words: sus4 replaces the third with the fourth, sus2 replaces it with the second, add9 keeps the third and adds the ninth. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.
teaches: embellishing a strum by moving one finger

studies.title: Strumming: Offbeat Chops
studies.goal: Short chords on the offbeats with silence on the beats
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, Am (x-x-7-5-5-x) and D (x-x-7-7-7-x) on strings 4-2, 2 bars each. Chop on the and of every beat (or on 2 and 4 in half-time feel) and mute at once by releasing the fretting pressure. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Strumming: Sixteenth-Note Funk
studies.goal: A constant sixteenth-note hand with chords on chosen sixteenths and muted strums elsewhere
studies.spec: 8 bars, 4/4, E9 (x-7-6-7-7-7) only. The hand moves in sixteenths all the time; play the chord on a written pattern of sixteenths and muted (scratch) strums on the rest. Two different 2-bar patterns, each repeated. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: 12-Bar Blues Shuffle in A
studies.goal: Play the 12-bar blues form with a shuffle rhythm
studies.spec: 12 bars, 4/4, swung eighths (long-short), played twice. Form: A A A A | D D A A | E D A E. Shuffle figure on two strings: A bars, the open string 5 (A) with string 4 fret 2 (E) alternating with string 4 fret 4 (F#); D bars, the open string 4 (D) with string 3 fret 2 (A) alternating with string 3 fret 4 (B); E bars, the open string 6 (E) with string 5 fret 2 (B) alternating with string 5 fret 4 (C#). The last E bar is the turnaround back to the top.

studies.title: 12-Bar Blues Shuffle in E (quick change)
studies.goal: The 12-bar blues in E, with the quick change to IV in bar 2
studies.spec: 12 bars, 4/4, swung eighths, played twice. Form: E A E E | A A E E | B7 A E B7. Shuffle on E and A as in st-blues-shuffle-a (E: the open string 6 (E) with string 5 fret 2 (B) and string 5 fret 4 (C#); A: the open string 5 (A) with string 4 fret 2 (E) and string 4 fret 4 (F#)); B7 bars strummed as B7 (x21202).

studies.title: Blues Turnarounds in E and A
studies.goal: Two classic-style turnarounds, each leading back to the top of the form
studies.spec: Two 2-bar turnarounds (bars 11-12 of a 12-bar). In E: over the open string 6, play a line descending by half steps on string 3, string 3 fret 7 (D), string 3 fret 6 (C#), string 3 fret 5 (C), string 3 fret 4 (B), each with the open string 1 (E), one per beat in swung eighths; bar 12: B7 (x21202). In A: over the open string 5, the same idea on string 4, string 4 fret 5 (G), string 4 fret 4 (F#), string 4 fret 3 (F), string 4 fret 2 (E), each with the open string 1; bar 12: E7 (020100). Both lines run b7, 6, b6, 5 of the key. Then a full 12-bar chorus using each one. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Minor Blues in A

studies.spec: 12 bars, 4/4, straight or slow swing. Form: Am7 Am7 Am7 Am7 | Dm7 Dm7 Am7 Am7 | E7 Dm7 Am7 E7. Shapes Am7 (x02010), Dm7 (xx0211), E7 (020100). Melody in A minor pentatonic box 1, with a written rhythm guitar part. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Fingerstyle Blues in E (steady thumb)

studies.spec: 12 bars, 4/4, E blues. The thumb plays the open string 6 (E) in steady quarter notes (palm-muted lightly) for E bars, the open string 5 (A) for A bars, string 5 fret 2 (B) for B bars; the fingers play an E minor pentatonic melody with slides on strings 1-3 in open position, including the blue note: string 3 fret 3 (Bb). Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Ragtime Blues in C

studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, progression C | C | A7 | A7 | D7 | D7 | G7 | G7, twice, the ragtime cycle of dominant sevenths (I, VI7, II7, V7). Shapes C (x32010), A7 (x02020), D7 (xx0212), G7 (320001). Thumb alternates bass strings on every beat; syncopated melody on strings 1-3. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Power Chords: Open Riff
studies.goal: Two-finger power chords and a first rock riff
studies.spec: 8 bars, 4/4, E minor, eighth-note downstrokes. Shapes E5 (022xxx), A5 (x022xx), D5 (xx023x), then the movable G5 (355xxx) and C5 (x355xx). Write an original riff that moves between them with rests. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Power Chords: Palm-Muted Gallop
studies.goal: The gallop rhythm (eighth plus two sixteenths) with palm muting
studies.spec: 8 bars, 4/4, E minor. Palm-muted gallop on the open string 6 (E) alternating with accented unmuted chords A5 (577xxx), G5 (355xxx), C5 (x355xx), D5 (x577xx). Strict down-down-up picking for the gallop. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

Box 1 notes: string 6 fret 5 (A), string 6 fret 8 (C), string 5 fret 5 (D), string 5 fret 7 (E), string 4 fret 5 (G), string 4 fret 7 (A), string 3 fret 5 (C), string 3 fret 7 (D), string 2 fret 5 (E), string 2 fret 8 (G), string 1 fret 5 (A), string 1 fret 8 (C). Fingers 1 and 3 or 1 and 4, one finger per fret. Include one hammer-on. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

Box 2 notes: string 6 fret 8 (C), string 6 fret 10 (D), string 5 fret 7 (E), string 5 fret 10 (G), string 4 fret 7 (A), string 4 fret 10 (C), string 3 fret 7 (D), string 3 fret 9 (E), string 2 fret 8 (G), string 2 fret 10 (A), string 1 fret 8 (C), string 1 fret 10 (D). Box 3 notes: string 6 fret 10 (D), string 6 fret 12 (E), string 5 fret 10 (G), string 5 fret 12 (A), string 4 fret 10 (C), string 4 fret 12 (D), string 3 fret 9 (E), string 3 fret 12 (G), string 2 fret 10 (A), string 2 fret 13 (C), string 1 fret 10 (D), string 1 fret 12 (E). studies.title: Pentatonic Across the Neck
studies.goal: Connect the five A minor pentatonic boxes into one map of the neck
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, over Am7: a melody that starts in box 5 (frets 2-5), climbs through boxes 1 (frets 5-8), 2, 3 and 4 (frets 12-15) by slides, then comes back down. Then the same 16 bars over a C (x32010) groove: the same notes now sound as C major pentatonic. studies.title: Lick: Hammer-Ons
studies.goal: Sound a second note by hammering a finger down, without picking it
studies.spec: 8 bars, 4/4, E minor pentatonic in open position. Hammer-ons from open strings: the open string 4 to string 4 fret 2 (E), the open string 3 to string 3 fret 2 (A), the open string 2 to string 2 fret 3 (D), the open string 1 to string 1 fret 3 (G). Pick only the first note of each pair. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Lick: Pull-Offs
studies.goal: Sound a lower note by plucking the string with the finger as it leaves
studies.spec: 8 bars, 4/4, E minor pentatonic in open position: string 1 fret 3 (G) pulled off to the open string 1, string 2 fret 3 (D) pulled off to the open string 2, string 3 fret 2 (A) pulled off to the open string 3. Then combine with hammer-ons into trills. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Lick: Slides
studies.goal: Move to a new note by sliding the fretting finger
studies.spec: 8 bars, 4/4, A minor pentatonic: slides from string 3 fret 7 (D) to string 3 fret 9 (E), from string 2 fret 8 (G) to string 2 fret 10 (A), and a long shift slide on string 4 from fret 5 (G) to fret 10 (C). Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Lick: Bends in Tune
studies.goal: Bend a string up to an exact target pitch
studies.spec: 8 bars, 4/4, A minor pentatonic box 1. Whole-step bends: string 3 fret 7 (D) up to the pitch of string 3 fret 9 (E), and string 2 fret 8 (G) up to the pitch of string 2 fret 10 (A); one half-step bend from string 2 fret 8 (G) to the pitch of string 2 fret 9 (G#) over an E7 bar. Before each bend, play the target fret so the ear (and the microphone) know the goal. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Lick: Vibrato
studies.goal: Bring held notes to life with an even, in-time vibrato
studies.spec: 8 bars, 4/4, slow A minor blues. Long notes on string 1 fret 5 (A), string 2 fret 8 (G) and string 3 fret 7 (D), each with vibrato: first 2 waves per beat, then 3, then 4. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Harmonics Melody
studies.goal: Play a melody using only natural harmonics
studies.spec: 8 bars, 4/4, G major, with only natural harmonics on strings 4, 3 and 2: over fret 12 they sound D, G and B, over fret 7 they sound A, D and F#, over fret 5 they sound D, G and B two octaves above the open strings. Teacher part: G and D chords. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Lick: Tapping Arpeggios
studies.goal: Tap with the picking hand to play wide arpeggios on one string
studies.spec: 8 bars, 4/4, triplet eighths, all on string 1. Am: tap string 1 fret 12 (E), pull off to string 1 fret 5 (A), hammer string 1 fret 8 (C). F: tap string 1 fret 13 (F), pull to fret 5 (A), hammer fret 8 (C). G: tap string 1 fret 15 (G), pull to string 1 fret 7 (B), hammer string 1 fret 10 (D). E: tap string 1 fret 12 (E), pull to string 1 fret 4 (G#), hammer string 1 fret 7 (B). Two bars per chord, Am F G E. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Fingerstyle: p i m a
studies.goal: Assign the thumb to the bass and i, m, a to strings 3, 2 and 1
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, eighth notes. C (x32010), Am (x02210), Dm (xx0231), G7 (320001), 4 bars each. The thumb plays the root (string 5 for C and Am, string 4 for Dm, string 6 for G7), i string 3, m string 2, a string 1. Patterns (eight eighths per bar): p-i-m-a twice (bars 1-8), p-a-m-i twice (bars 9-12), p-i-m-a-m-i-m-i (bars 13-16), and in bars 15-16 a pinch of p and a together on beat 1 in place of the first p. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Fingerstyle: p i m a m i in 3/4
studies.goal: A flowing six-note arpeggio that fills a 3/4 bar
studies.spec: 16 bars, 3/4, eighths: p-i-m-a-m-i each bar. Am (x02210), Dm (xx0231), E (022100), Am, with the thumb on string 5, 4, 6 and 5. Bars 9-16: a melody note on string 1 on beat 1 of each bar, played by a together with the thumb (a pinch). Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Travis Picking
studies.goal: An alternating-bass thumb that never stops, with fingers picking between
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4. Thumb on every beat, alternating: C (x32010) on string 5 fret 3 (C), string 4, string 6 fret 3 (G), string 4 (finger 3 moves between strings 5 and 6); G7 (320001) on string 6 fret 3 (G) and string 4; Am (x02210) on the open string 5 (A) and string 4 fret 2 (E). Fingers in eighths between the thumb notes: i on string 2 on the and of 1 and the and of 3, m on string 1 on the and of 2 and the and of 4. Bars 9-16: the same with a pinch (thumb and m together) on beat 1. Light palm mute on the bass. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Travis Picking with a Melody
studies.goal: Carry an original melody on top of the Travis pattern
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, C major: C (x32010), F (xx3211), G7 (320001), Am (x02210). The thumb keeps the alternating bass from st-travis-picking; the fingers play a singable original melody on strings 1-2, sometimes on the beat (pinched with the thumb), sometimes syncopated. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Thumb-Lead Melody with Brush Strums
studies.goal: Melody on the bass strings with the thumb, brush strums on the top strings with the index
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, C major. The thumb plays an original melody on strings 6-4 in first position (C D E F G A B), with i brushing strings 3-1 of the current chord on the offbeats; chords C (x32010), F (xx3211), G7 (320001). Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Triad Arpeggios in First Position
studies.goal: Play the six major and minor chords of C major as arpeggios, one octave from each root
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, eighth notes, alternate picking: C (C E G), Dm (D F A), Em (E G B), F (F A C), G (G B D), Am (A C E), each up and down from its root in first position (B diminished waits for st-arpeggio-sevenths), then a 4-bar melody built from them. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Seventh-Chord Arpeggios in C
studies.goal: Arpeggiate the seven diatonic seventh chords of C major
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, eighth notes in fifth position: Cmaj7 (C E G B), Dm7 (D F A C), Em7 (E G B D), Fmaj7 (F A C E), G7 (G B D F), Am7 (A C E G), Bm7b5 (B D F A), one bar up and down each, then an 8-bar melody over Dm7 G7 Cmaj7 that outlines them. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Sweep-Picked Arpeggios
studies.goal: Play arpeggios with one stroke per direction across the strings
studies.spec: 8 bars, 4/4, sextuplets or triplets. Three-string shapes: Am (string 3 fret 14 (A), string 2 fret 13 (C), string 1 fret 12 (E)) and C (string 3 fret 12 (G), string 2 fret 13 (C), string 1 fret 12 (E)); five-string Am: string 5 fret 12 (A), string 4 fret 14 (E), string 3 fret 14 (A), string 2 fret 13 (C), string 1 fret 12 (E), up to string 1 fret 17 (A) and back. Each note must stop as the next one sounds (roll the finger, lift behind). Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: First Barre: F
studies.goal: Get a clean full barre chord, F at the first fret
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, half-note strums: C (x32010) to F (133211) and back, 2 bars each; then Am (x02210) to F. Fallback for bad days: Fmaj7 (xx3210). Check the barre string by string before each change.

studies.title: Barre Shapes: E, Em, A and Am Shapes
studies.goal: Move the four main barre shapes along the neck
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4. E shape: F (133211), G (355433), A (577655). Em shape: Fm (133111), Gm (355333), Am (577555). A shape: Bb (x13331), B (x24442), C (x35553). Am shape: Bm (x24432), Cm (x35543). One bar each with a steady strum, naming the root on string 6 or 5 aloud.

studies.title: Barre Progression: I-vi-IV-V
studies.goal: Use barre chords in a real progression and in other keys
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, folk strum. In A: A (x02220), F#m (244222), D (xx0232), E (022100). Then in C with barres: C (x35553), Am (577555), F (133211), G (355433). Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: CAGED: One Chord, Five Shapes
studies.goal: Find C and then G in five shapes up the neck
studies.spec: 20 bars, 4/4, one shape per bar (twice up and down). C: C (x32010) in the C shape, A-shape C (x35553), G-shape C (875558), E-shape C (8-10-10-9-8-8), D-shape C (x-x-10-12-13-12), and the C shape an octave up, C (x-15-14-12-13-12). G: G (320003), E-shape G (355433), D-shape G (x-x-5-7-8-7), C-shape G (x-10-9-7-8-7), A-shape G (x-10-12-12-12-10). Name where the root sits in each shape.

studies.title: CAGED: The Major Scale in Five Positions
studies.goal: Play C major in the five CAGED positions and join them
studies.spec: 20 bars, 4/4, eighth notes: C major from root to root and back in each position (C shape frets 0-3, A shape frets 2-6, G shape frets 4-8, E shape frets 7-10, D shape frets 9-13), then a 4-bar original melody in each position.

studies.title: CAGED: One Melody Everywhere
studies.goal: Play the same 8-bar melody in all five positions
studies.spec: An original 8-bar melody in C major, 4/4, played five times, once in each CAGED position, each with the matching chord shape from st-caged-chords as accompaniment. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Mode Study: A Ionian (major)
studies.goal: Hear the major scale as a mode: its colour is the major seventh, G#
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, the vamp changing every 2 bars; a melody of quarter and eighth notes that lands on the colour note on a strong beat at least four times and ends on A. Backing part included. A Ionian: A B C# D E F# G#. Vamp Amaj7 (x02120) to D (xx0232): the Amaj7 carries the G#, and the D (not D#) rules out Lydian. Colour note: G#. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Mode Study: A Dorian
studies.goal: Minor with a bright sixth: F#
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, the vamp changing every 2 bars; a melody of quarter and eighth notes that lands on the colour note on a strong beat at least four times and ends on A. Backing part included. A Dorian: A B C D E F# G. Vamp Am (x02210) to D (xx0232); the D major chord carries the F#. Colour note: F#. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Mode Study: A Mixolydian
studies.goal: Major with a flat seventh: G natural
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, the vamp changing every 2 bars; a melody of quarter and eighth notes that lands on the colour note on a strong beat at least four times and ends on A. Backing part included. A Mixolydian: A B C# D E F# G. Vamp A (x02220) to G (320003). Colour note: G. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Mode Study: A Aeolian (natural minor)
studies.goal: The natural minor and its flat sixth: F
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, the vamp changing every 2 bars; a melody of quarter and eighth notes that lands on the colour note on a strong beat at least four times and ends on A. Backing part included. A Aeolian: A B C D E F G. Vamp Am (x02210), F (133211), G (320003): two bars of Am, one each of F and G. Colour note: F. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Mode Study: A Phrygian
studies.goal: Minor with a flat second: Bb, the Spanish-sounding mode
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, the vamp changing every 2 bars; a melody of quarter and eighth notes that lands on the colour note on a strong beat at least four times and ends on A. Backing part included. A Phrygian: A Bb C D E F G. Vamp Am (x02210) to Bb (x13331). Colour note: Bb, resolving down to A. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Mode Study: A Lydian
studies.goal: Major with a raised fourth: D#, the dreamy mode
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, the vamp changing every 2 bars; a melody of quarter and eighth notes that lands on the colour note on a strong beat at least four times and ends on A. Backing part included. A Lydian: A B C# D# E F# G#. Vamp A (x02220) to B (x24442). Colour note: D#. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Mode Study: A Locrian
studies.goal: The unstable mode: flat second and flat fifth (Bb and Eb)
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, the vamp changing every 2 bars; a melody of quarter and eighth notes that lands on the colour note on a strong beat at least four times and ends on A. Backing part included. A Locrian: A Bb C D Eb F G. Vamp Am7b5 (x0101x) to Bbmaj7 (x1323x). Colour notes: Eb and Bb. Explain why songs rarely stay here: its home chord is diminished. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Jazz Comping: Shell Voicings on ii-V-I
studies.goal: Comp a ii-V-I in C with three-note shells
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, swing. Dm7 (x535xx), G7 (3x34xx), Cmaj7 (x324xx): root, third and seventh only. Bars 1-8: four-to-the-bar quarter notes, short; bars 9-16: the Charleston rhythm (beat 1 and the and of 2). Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Jazz Comping: Drop-2 Voicings
studies.goal: Voice-lead a ii-V-I on the top four strings
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, swing. Dm7 (xx3535), G7 (xx3433), Cmaj7 (xx2413): each note moves as little as possible (F stays, C goes to B, D stays, A goes to G; then F to E, B stays, D to C, G stays). Then the same in F by moving every shape up 5 frets. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Jazz Comping: Minor ii-V-i
studies.goal: Comp the minor ii-V-i in A minor
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, swing or bossa. Bm7b5 (x2323x), E7 (xx2434), Am7 (xx2213). Then an 8-bar melody over it using A harmonic minor over the E7 (G#). Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Bossa-Style Groove
studies.goal: A Brazilian-style syncopated fingerstyle comp
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, Am7 (5x555x) and D7 (x5453x), 2 bars each. The thumb plays the root on beats 1 and 3; the fingers pluck the upper notes in a written two-bar syncopated pattern (for example bar 1: beat 1, the and of 2, beat 4; bar 2: the and of 1, beat 3, the and of 3). Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Chord Melody: First Ballad
studies.goal: Put the melody on top and the chords underneath
studies.spec: An original 16-bar ballad in C major, 4/4: melody on strings 1-2, chords C, Am, F, G7, Em, Dm placed under the melody on strong beats with the melody note always the highest. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.
teaches: voicing with the melody on top

studies.title: Chord Melody: Jazz Ballad with Reharmonisation
studies.goal: A chord-melody arrangement with secondary dominants and a tritone substitution
studies.spec: An original 32-bar AABA ballad in F major, 4/4: melody on top, chords Fmaj7, Dm7, Gm7, C7, plus secondary dominants (D7 to Gm7) and one tritone substitution (Gb7 for C7). Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Reading: First Position in C
studies.goal: Read notes on strings 1-3 in first position
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, C major, quarter and half notes, range G to G (open string 3 to string 1 fret 3 (G)), stepwise with small skips. No ties or dotted notes. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Reading: First Position in G
studies.goal: Read across all six strings, with F#
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, G major, eighth notes added, range string 6 fret 3 (G) to string 1 fret 3 (G); F# on string 4 fret 4 (F#) and string 1 fret 2 (F#). Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Reading: Sharps and Dotted Rhythms
studies.goal: Read in D and A major in first position, with dotted rhythms and ties
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, D major then A major: C# on string 5 fret 4 (C#) and string 2 fret 2 (C#), G# on string 3 fret 1 (G#); dotted quarters, ties across the bar line. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Reading: Second Position
studies.goal: Read in second position (finger 1 on fret 2)
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, A major and F# minor, finger 1 on fret 2 throughout, no open strings. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Reading: Fifth Position and Flats
studies.goal: Read in fifth position, in C major and F major
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4, C major then F major (Bb on string 3 fret 3 in first position becomes string 4 fret 8 (Bb) here), finger 1 on fret 5. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Reading: Seventh Position
studies.goal: Read in seventh position, G major and E minor
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4 and 6/8 sections, finger 1 on fret 7, sixteenth notes in places. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Reading: Shifting Through the Neck
studies.goal: Read a piece that moves through positions I, V, VII, IX and XII
studies.spec: 32 bars, changing meter (4/4, 3/4, 6/8), keys with up to four sharps or flats; fingering suggestions only at shifts. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Duet: An Original Round
studies.goal: Play a round in two parts with the teacher
studies.spec: An original 8-bar tune in G major, 4/4, designed as a round: the second voice enters after 2 bars, so every 2-bar segment must fit over the same harmony, G for one bar, D for the next. Notes in first position on strings 4-1. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Duet: Baroque-Style Duo in D minor
studies.goal: Hold your line against an independent bass line
studies.spec: An original 24-bar binary-form duo in D minor, 3/4 (minuet style): student plays the upper voice in first position, the teacher the bass line. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Andalusian Cadence with Rasgueado
studies.goal: The Spanish descending progression Am G F E with flamenco strums
studies.spec: 16 bars, 3/4. Am (x02210), G (320003), F (xx3211), E (022100), one bar each, four times; ends on E (the home chord of E Phrygian). Rasgueado (four-finger fan) on beat 1 of each bar, thumb strokes after. A short melody in E Phrygian in bars 9-16. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Flamenco Rhythm: the 12-Beat Cycle
studies.goal: Feel the 12-beat cycle of solea with accents on 3, 6, 8, 10 and 12
studies.spec: Four cycles of 12 beats, accents on 3, 6, 8, 10 and 12, on E (022100) and F (xx3211). Rasgueado on the accents, thumb strokes elsewhere; a closing falseta (short melody) in E Phrygian. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Bluegrass Rhythm and the G Run
studies.goal: Bass-strum rhythm with a G-run ending
studies.spec: 16 bars, 4/4: G (320003), C (x32010), D (xx0232), with bass on 1 and 3 and strums on 2 and 4. Each 8-bar phrase ends with a G-run style ending in eighth notes: the open string 3 (G), string 4 fret 2 (E), the open string 4 (D), then a hammer-on from the open string 5 to string 5 fret 2 (B), landing on string 6 fret 3 (G) on beat 1. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: DADGAD Air
studies.goal: A Celtic-style air in the DADGAD tuning
studies.spec: Retune to D A D G A D (strings 6 to 1). An original 16-bar air in D, 3/4, using open strings as drones and ringing intervals; the tab must state the tuning and every fret number must be checked in that tuning. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Open G Slide Blues
studies.goal: Slide guitar in open G tuning
studies.spec: Retune to D G D G B D (strings 6 to 1). An original 12-bar blues in G with a slide on finger 3 or 4: whole-chord slides at the 12th, 5th and 7th frets (G, C, D chords in this tuning) and single-note slide melody on strings 1-3, muting behind the slide. Every fret number must be checked in this tuning. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Two-Voice Invention for Solo Guitar
studies.goal: Play true two-part counterpoint on one guitar
studies.spec: An original 24-bar two-voice invention in E minor, 4/4: a short subject imitated between bass and treble, a modulation to G major and back, playable in positions I to VII. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Concert Tremolo Etude
studies.goal: Sustain a tremolo melody across a full piece
studies.spec: An original 40-bar tremolo etude in D minor/D major, 3/4: p a m i tremolo throughout, melody on strings 1 and 2 up to the 12th position, bass moving under it. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

studies.title: Fugue Exposition for Solo Guitar
studies.goal: Three entries of a fugue subject on one guitar
studies.spec: An original fugue exposition in D minor, 4/4, about 24 bars: subject, answer at the fifth, third entry, with a countersubject; drop D tuning allowed. Original material: it must not quote or imitate any existing song, riff or lick closely enough to be recognised.

technique.title: Posture: Sitting and Standing
technique.pattern: Sitting, casual: the guitar's waist on the right thigh (left thigh for left-handed players), neck pointing slightly up, back upright, shoulders down. Sitting, classical: left foot on a footstool or a support under the guitar, guitar on the left thigh, headstock about eye level. Standing: set the strap so the guitar sits where it did when seated. Fretting thumb behind the neck, roughly opposite finger 2; no sharp bend in either wrist. Check with one slow open-chord strum per beat for one minute.
watchFor: hunching over to look at the fretboard
a sharply bent fretting wrist
the thumb squeezing hard from behind the neck
raised shoulders

technique.title: Play Without Pain
technique.pattern: Practise in blocks of 20 to 30 minutes with a short break between them, and build total time up gradually. Sore fingertips in the first weeks are normal; aching joints, numbness, tingling or sharp pain are not: stop, rest, and see a doctor or physiotherapist if it lasts. Use the lightest pressure that gives a clean note. Keep the fretting-hand nails short. Every few minutes, freeze and check jaw, shoulders, fretting thumb and picking wrist for tension.
watchFor: playing through pain
long sessions with no breaks
jumping straight to big stretches or long barre work
pressing harder than needed (use just enough pressure to stop the buzz)

technique.title: Five-Minute Warm-Up
technique.pattern: Minute 1: gentle down-up picking on open strings (eighths). Minute 2: the chromatic spider (tech-spider) at a slow tempo. Minute 3: slow changes between two easy chords. Minute 4: gentle hammer-ons and pull-offs. Minute 5: a slow scale. Never stretch to discomfort; if your hands are cold, warm them first.
watchFor: starting with your hardest piece or fastest tempo
stretching to the point of discomfort
pressing harder than needed (use just enough pressure to stop the buzz)

technique.title: Cool-Down
technique.pattern: End each session with two minutes of slow, easy playing (a slow melody or open-chord arpeggios), then let the hands hang loose and shake them out gently. Note one thing that felt tense today.
watchFor: stopping abruptly after fast playing
ending on the hardest exercise

technique.title: Holding the Pick
technique.pattern: Hold the pick between the pad of the thumb and the side of the index finger near its last joint (the one closest to the tip), with 2 to 3 mm showing. Downstrokes on the open string 6, quarter notes, 4 bars; then strings 5 to 1. The motion comes from the wrist, not the elbow.
watchFor: gripping too tightly
too much pick showing
moving from the elbow
the pick turning in the fingers

technique.title: Alternate Picking on Open Strings
technique.pattern: Down-up eighth notes on the open string 1 for 2 bars, then strings 2 to 6, then back. Then triplets (down-up-down, up-down-up), then sixteenths. Strictly alternate: down on the beat. The ladder is for eighth notes; when you move on to triplets and then sixteenths, start again at 60.
watchFor: two downstrokes in a row
big pick movements
the hand speeding up between clicks

technique.title: Constant Strumming Motion
technique.pattern: On one chord (Em (022000)), the hand moves down on every beat and up on every "and", whether or not it touches the strings. Pattern: down (1), down (2), up (and), miss (3), up (and), down (4), up (and). 8 bars, then switch to G (320003).
watchFor: stopping the hand on the missed strokes
strumming from the elbow
upstrokes hitting all six strings hard

technique.title: Strum Only the Right Strings
technique.pattern: D (xx0232) strums strings 4-1 only, A (x02220) strings 5-1, E (022100) all six. Two bars each, cycling D-A-E; aim the first downstroke at the right string.
watchFor: hitting the open string 6 under a D chord
looking at the picking hand instead of listening

technique.title: Tuning by Ear (Fifth-Fret Method)
technique.pattern: Tune string 6 to the app's tuner or a reference tone. Then each string from the one below it: string 6 fret 5 (A) gives the pitch for the open string 5 (A); string 5 fret 5 (D) for the open string 4 (D); string 4 fret 5 (G) for the open string 3 (G); string 3 fret 4 (B), not fret 5, for the open string 2 (B); string 2 fret 5 (E) for the open string 1 (E). Play the fretted note, then the open string, and listen for the wobble (beats): it slows down as the pitches get closer and stops when they match. Always tune up to the note: if a string is sharp, loosen it below the note and come back up. Check with a G (320003) chord and with the tuner.
watchFor: using fret 5 on string 3 (string 3 to string 2 needs fret 4)
tuning down to the note instead of up to it
turning the wrong peg: pluck while you turn and follow the pitch
winding a string far above its note, which can break it: turn slowly

technique.title: Subdivision Switch
technique.pattern: On Em (022000), two bars each of quarters, eighths, triplets and sixteenths, then back down, without stopping. Metronome on quarter notes.
watchFor: triplets drifting into eighths
speeding up on the sixteenths

technique.title: Using a Capo
technique.pattern: Clip the capo straight across, just behind a fret wire (on the headstock side, as close to the wire as it sits), with just enough pressure to stop buzzing. A capo can pull strings sharp, so check every string with the tuner after clipping it on. Play G (320003), C (x32010) and D (xx0232) with the capo at fret 2: the shapes keep their names, but they sound a whole step higher, as A, D and E. With the capo at fret 5 the same shapes sound as C, F and G. Each fret of capo raises everything one half step. Play one song's chords at three capo positions and choose the one that suits your voice.
watchFor: the capo in the middle of the fret space or on top of the fret wire (buzzing or sharp notes)
a capo clamped so hard that it bends the strings sharp
forgetting to retune after clipping it on
telling other players the shape name instead of the chord that actually sounds

technique.title: Palm Muting
technique.pattern: Rest the edge of the picking hand on the strings right where they leave the bridge saddle. Downstroke eighths on E5 (022xxx): 2 bars muted, 2 bars open. Move the hand 1 cm toward the neck for a heavier mute, then back.
watchFor: muting so far toward the neck that the pitch disappears
lifting the hand on accents
a burning forearm: all-downstroke speed comes from a loose wrist, not more force; stop and shake the arm out

technique.title: Alternate Picking: Chromatic
technique.pattern: Frets 5-6-7-8 with fingers 1-2-3-4 on each string from 6 to 1 and back, one note per pick stroke, strictly down-up starting with a down. Eighths up the ladder; start again at 60 when you switch to sixteenths.
watchFor: restarting with a downstroke on every string
pick strokes much larger than needed

technique.title: Alternate Picking: G Major, Two Octaves
technique.pattern: G major in first position, two octaves up and down: string 6 fret 3 (G); the open string 5 (A), string 5 fret 2 (B), string 5 fret 3 (C); the open string 4 (D), string 4 fret 2 (E), string 4 fret 4 (F#); the open string 3 (G), string 3 fret 2 (A); the open string 2 (B), string 2 fret 1 (C), string 2 fret 3 (D); the open string 1 (E), string 1 fret 2 (F#), string 1 fret 3 (G). Eighths, strictly alternate.
watchFor: losing alternation at string changes
open strings ringing over the next note

technique.title: String Crossing Both Ways
technique.pattern: Two-note figures repeated for one bar each, eighths, strict alternation. Pattern A: string 3 fret 5 (C) with a downstroke, then string 2 fret 5 (E) with an upstroke. Pattern B: string 3 fret 5 (C) with an upstroke, then string 2 fret 5 (E) with a downstroke. Then the same on strings 2 and 1, and 4 and 3. Practise both orders: each makes the pick escape a different way.
watchFor: catching the wrong string
one pattern much weaker than the other
a tense, locked wrist

technique.title: Economy Picking
technique.pattern: Three notes per string up G major (tech-legato-3nps fingering), picked down-up-down on each string, with the change to the next string taken by continuing the downstroke (one sweeping motion). Descending: up-down-up, continuing the upstroke across the change.
watchFor: two separate strokes where one sweep is meant
uneven note lengths at the sweep

technique.title: Sweep Picking: Three Strings
technique.pattern: A minor triad: string 3 fret 14 (A), string 2 fret 13 (C), string 1 fret 12 (E) in one downstroke, then back in one upstroke; then C: string 3 fret 12 (G), string 2 fret 13 (C), string 1 fret 12 (E). Triplets. Each note must stop as the next sounds: lift each finger just after its note.
watchFor: notes ringing together like a strummed chord
separate strokes instead of one sweep
rushing the first note

technique.title: Sweep Picking: Five Strings
technique.pattern: A minor across five strings: string 5 fret 12 (A), string 4 fret 14 (E), string 3 fret 14 (A), string 2 fret 13 (C), string 1 fret 12 (E), hammer or slide to string 1 fret 17 (A), then back down. Sextuplets or sixteenths.
watchFor: the two notes at fret 14 ringing together
unequal timing between strings
string noise from the unused strings

technique.title: String Skipping
technique.pattern: Octave shapes first: string 6 fret 5 (A) to string 4 fret 7 (A), string 5 fret 5 (D) to string 3 fret 7 (D), alternate picking. Then A minor pentatonic box 1 played on string pairs 6-4, 5-3, 4-2 and 3-1 (skipping the string between).
watchFor: the skipped string ringing
the pick arcing too high over the skipped string

technique.title: Octave Shapes with Muting
technique.pattern: Root on string 6 with finger 1, the octave two frets higher on string 4 with finger 3 or 4: string 6 fret 3 (G) with string 4 fret 5 (G). Root on string 5, octave on string 3: string 5 fret 3 (C) with string 3 fret 5 (C). From string 4 to string 2, and string 3 to string 1, the octave is three frets higher because of the B string: string 4 fret 5 (G) with string 2 fret 8 (G), string 3 fret 5 (C) with string 1 fret 8 (C). Finger 1 lies lightly against the string in between to mute it, so you can strum all three strings or pick both notes together. Play the G major scale in octaves on strings 6 and 4, then a short melody of your own.
watchFor: the muted middle string sounding
open strings ringing under the octave
finger 1 pressing the middle string down instead of touching it

technique.title: Tremolo Picking
technique.pattern: Constant fast alternate picking on one note (the open string 1, then string 2 fret 5 (E)), sixteenths up the ladder (thirty-seconds only at half the ladder tempo or less), changing notes on the beat without breaking the motion.
watchFor: tension in the forearm
the motion stopping at note changes
uneven volume
a burning or cramping forearm: stop at once; work in 30-second bursts with rests between

technique.title: Speed Bursts
technique.pattern: A four-note figure, string 1 fret 8 (C), string 1 fret 7 (B), string 1 fret 5 (A), string 2 fret 8 (G): play it once in sixteenths at a tempo just above your comfortable top speed, then rest for a beat; then two figures in a row, rest; then four. Return to the comfortable tempo and notice how easy it feels.
watchFor: bursting with tension instead of loose hands
playing long bursts before short ones are clean

technique.title: Picking-Hand Muting of the Low Strings
technique.pattern: While playing single notes on strings 1-3, let the side of the picking palm rest on strings 4-6 so they stay silent; then move the palm as the notes move to lower strings.
watchFor: the low strings ringing in sympathy
the palm muting the string being played

technique.title: Hybrid Picking
technique.pattern: Pick between thumb and index; middle (m) and ring (a) fingers free. Over C (x32010): pick on string 5, m on string 2, pick on string 4, a on string 1, eighths. Then pinch pick on string 5 together with m on string 2.
watchFor: the pick grip loosening when the fingers pluck
fingers plucking too hard (snapping strings)

technique.title: Rasgueado Basics
technique.pattern: Four-stroke fan: with a loosely closed hand, flick out the little finger (written c or e), then a, m and i downward across the strings one after another, then an upstroke with i. Count c, a, m and i as four sixteenths (one beat) and put the upstroke on the next beat. On E (022100), then Am (x02210).
watchFor: all fingers flicking at once (one stroke instead of four)
the wrist moving instead of the fingers
scraping strokes
an aching wrist or back of the hand: flick from the finger joints with the wrist loose, and keep the first sessions short

technique.title: Free-Stroke Arpeggios (p i m a)
technique.pattern: Over C (x32010): p on string 5, i on string 3, m on string 2, a on string 1. Patterns in eighths: p-i-m-a twice in a bar of 4/4, p-a-m-i twice in a bar of 4/4, p-i-m-a-m-i as a bar of 3/4, then p with i-m-a plucked together on every beat.
watchFor: the thumb plucking toward the palm instead of forward
fingers lifting far from the strings
uneven volume between fingers

technique.title: Rest Stroke Scale (i-m)
technique.pattern: Rest stroke (apoyando): after plucking, the finger comes to rest on the next string toward string 6. C major scale on strings 3-1 in first position, strictly alternating i and m, quarters then eighths.
watchFor: using the same finger twice in a row
the hand bouncing
thin tone from plucking upward

technique.title: Thumb Independence
technique.pattern: The thumb plays steady quarter notes alternating the open string 6 (E) and string 4 fret 2 (E) under E (022100) while i plays off-beat eighths on string 3; then i and m play a simple syncopated melody on strings 1-2 over the same thumb.
watchFor: the thumb following the fingers into syncopation
bass notes too loud

technique.title: Travis Thumb, Muted
technique.pattern: Palm-mute strings 4-6 lightly; on C (x32010) the thumb alternates string 5, string 4, string 6, string 4 on every beat for 2 minutes, steady as a clock; then add a pinch (thumb plus m on string 2) on beat 1.
watchFor: the thumb rushing
missing the move to string 6
the mute killing the bass completely

technique.title: Classical Tremolo (p a m i)
technique.pattern: The thumb plays a bass note on strings 4-6, then a, m and i repeat one treble note on string 1: four even notes p-a-m-i per beat (sixteenths). First on the open string 1 over open bass strings, then with a moving melody on string 1.
watchFor: a gallop (uneven a-m-i)
the thumb too loud
tension in the hand

technique.title: Dynamic Control
technique.pattern: One arpeggio pattern played pp, p, mf, f, ff (one bar each), then a crescendo over 4 bars and a diminuendo over 4 bars. The microphone level meter shows the result.
watchFor: all levels sounding the same
speeding up when getting louder

technique.title: Chromatic Spider (1-2-3-4)
technique.pattern: One finger per fret in fifth position: on string 6, frets 5-6-7-8 with fingers 1-2-3-4; the same on strings 5 to 1; then 8-7-6-5 (fingers 4-3-2-1) on each string from 1 back to 6. Then move the whole pattern down one fret at a time toward first position, only as far as it stays comfortable: the frets get wider near the nut. Eighth notes.
watchFor: fingers flying far from the strings when lifted
pressing harder than needed (use just enough pressure to stop the buzz)
the thumb squeezing the neck
fingertips collapsing at the first joint
stretching for frets 1-4 before the hand is ready (stay higher up the neck for now)

technique.title: Finger Permutations: Starting with 1
technique.pattern: The six orders that start with finger 1: 1-2-3-4, 1-2-4-3, 1-3-2-4, 1-3-4-2, 1-4-2-3, 1-4-3-2. Each four times on one string (frets 5-8), then across all six strings. Eighths.
watchFor: other fingers lifting high while one finger plays
slowing down on the hard orders

technique.title: Finger Permutations: Starting with 2
technique.pattern: The six orders that start with finger 2: 2-1-3-4, 2-1-4-3, 2-3-1-4, 2-3-4-1, 2-4-1-3, 2-4-3-1. Each four times on one string (frets 5-8), then across all six strings.
watchFor: other fingers lifting high
tension in the fingers that are waiting

technique.title: Finger Permutations: Starting with 3 and 4
technique.pattern: The twelve orders that start with finger 3 or 4: 3-1-2-4, 3-1-4-2, 3-2-1-4, 3-2-4-1, 3-4-1-2, 3-4-2-1, 4-1-2-3, 4-1-3-2, 4-2-1-3, 4-2-3-1, 4-3-1-2, 4-3-2-1. Each four times on one string, then across strings. With tech-permutations-1 and -2 this covers all 24.
watchFor: finger 4 collapsing
fingers 3 and 4 moving together

technique.title: Anchored Fingers
technique.pattern: Keep fingers 1 and 2 pressed at frets 5 and 6 on string 4 while fingers 3 and 4 alternate at frets 7 and 8 on string 3; then hold 3 and 4 down and move 1 and 2. Repeat on every pair of neighbouring strings.
watchFor: the anchored fingers lifting
squeezing with the thumb to compensate
an ache at the base of fingers 3 and 4: work for 30 seconds at a time and stop at any ache, since this exercise strains hands that push it

technique.title: Hammer and Pull Chains
technique.pattern: Pick only the first note on each string: hammer frets 5-7-8 (fingers 1-3-4) going up across all strings, then pull 8-7-5 coming down. Every note equally loud.
watchFor: hammered notes much quieter than picked ones
pull-offs that just lift the finger instead of plucking

technique.title: Double Stops: Thirds and Sixths
technique.pattern: Thirds in G major on strings 3 and 2, both strings together, moving up the neck: the open strings 3 and 2 (G and B), then string 3 fret 2 (A) with string 2 fret 1 (C), string 3 fret 4 (B) with string 2 fret 3 (D), string 3 fret 5 (C) with string 2 fret 5 (E), string 3 fret 7 (D) with string 2 fret 7 (F#), string 3 fret 9 (E) with string 2 fret 8 (G), string 3 fret 11 (F#) with string 2 fret 10 (A), string 3 fret 12 (G) with string 2 fret 12 (B). Then sixths on strings 3 and 1 with string 2 muted by the underside of the finger on string 3: string 3 fret 4 (B) with string 1 fret 3 (G), string 3 fret 5 (C) with string 1 fret 5 (A), string 3 fret 7 (D) with string 1 fret 7 (B), string 3 fret 9 (E) with string 1 fret 8 (C), string 3 fret 11 (F#) with string 1 fret 10 (D), string 3 fret 12 (G) with string 1 fret 12 (E). Pick both strings at once (or pluck with thumb and finger), quarter notes, then eighths, then slide between neighbouring pairs.
watchFor: string 2 ringing during the sixths
one note of the pair louder than the other
pressing hard while sliding between pairs

technique.title: Trills
technique.pattern: On string 3 in fifth position, trill (rapid hammer-on and pull-off) each finger pair for 10 seconds: 1-2, 1-3, 1-4, 2-3, 2-4, 3-4. Count four notes per beat. Rest 20 seconds between pairs.
watchFor: the lower finger lifting
notes dying away after a few repetitions
a tired or aching hand: stop, because trills tire the small hand muscles quickly

technique.title: Three-Notes-per-String Legato
technique.pattern: G major, three notes per string from string 6 fret 3 (G): frets 3-5-7 on strings 6 and 5, string 4 fret 4 (F#), frets 5 and 7 on string 4, string 3 fret 4 (B), frets 5 and 7 on string 3, string 2 fret 5 (E), string 2 fret 7 (F#), string 2 fret 8 (G), string 1 fret 5 (A), string 1 fret 7 (B), string 1 fret 8 (C). Pick only the first note on each string, hammer the rest; descend with pull-offs.
watchFor: the first note of each string much louder than the rest
letting the hand drift where the pattern moves up a fret on strings 4 and 3

technique.title: Hammer-On from Nowhere
technique.pattern: Sound notes by hammering alone, with no picked note before: string 3 fret 7 (D), string 2 fret 8 (G), string 1 fret 5 (A), each hammered onto a silent string, then legato runs that start this way.
watchFor: weak, quiet notes
other strings ringing

technique.title: Gentle Stretch, Walking Down
technique.pattern: One finger per fret, 1-2-3-4, starting at frets 9-12 on string 3 and moving down one fret per repetition to frets 1-4. The gaps get wider toward the nut: never force; stop as soon as it feels like strain rather than effort, and try again another day.
watchFor: forcing the stretch
the thumb sliding over the top of the neck
pain (stop at once)

technique.title: Clean Position Shifts
technique.pattern: Up string 3 with a guide finger: string 3 fret 2 (A) with finger 1, string 3 fret 4 (B) with finger 3, glide finger 1 lightly to string 3 fret 5 (C), finger 3 on string 3 fret 7 (D), glide finger 1 to string 3 fret 9 (E). Then down. Quarters, then eighths.
watchFor: lifting off the string during the shift (a gap)
squeezing during the shift (a squeak)
arriving late

technique.title: Slides to a Target
technique.pattern: Slide finger 3 from string 3 fret 7 (D) to string 3 fret 9 (E) and back; then from string 2 fret 5 (E) to string 2 fret 8 (G). Arrive exactly on the beat, with steady pressure all the way.
watchFor: losing pressure mid-slide
overshooting the target fret

technique.title: Half-Step Bend in Tune
technique.pattern: Play the target first: string 2 fret 9 (G#). Then bend string 2 fret 8 (G) with finger 3 (fingers 1 and 2 behind it, helping) until it matches G#; hold for two beats; release. The microphone checks the held pitch: within 10 cents.
watchFor: bending with one finger alone
overshooting then settling
the pitch sinking while held

technique.title: Whole-Step Bend in Tune
technique.pattern: Target first: string 3 fret 9 (E). Bend string 3 fret 7 (D) up a whole step with finger 3, supported by 1 and 2, pushing the string toward the ceiling. Hold two beats on E; release. Then on string 2: target string 2 fret 10 (A), bend string 2 fret 8 (G). The microphone checks the held pitch: within 10 cents.
watchFor: bending flat (short of the target)
other strings ringing under the bend
pulling the string off the fretboard
forcing whole-step bends on an acoustic guitar with a wound string 3: bend half steps there, or practise on lighter strings

technique.title: Step-and-a-Half Bend
technique.pattern: Target first: string 2 fret 8 (G). Bend string 2 fret 5 (E) up three frets' worth until it matches G; hold; release. Use all three fingers and turn the wrist rather than pushing with the fingers alone.
watchFor: stopping short of the target
a wavering held pitch
sore fingertips or wrist: wide bends need light strings (an electric guitar), and a few minutes at a time

technique.title: Unison Bend
technique.pattern: Fret string 2 fret 5 (E) with finger 1 and string 3 fret 7 (D) with finger 3; pick both and bend string 3 until it matches the E: the two notes merge and the beating stops.
watchFor: the fretted E being pulled along by the bend
stopping while the notes still beat against each other

technique.title: Pre-Bend and Release
technique.pattern: Silently bend string 3 fret 7 (D) up to E, pick it, then release slowly back to D over one beat, in time. The microphone checks both the start (E) and the end (D).
watchFor: pre-bending to the wrong pitch
a sudden drop instead of a smooth release

technique.title: Bending Vibrato in Time
technique.pattern: On string 2 fret 8 (G) with finger 3: small repeated bends up about a quarter tone and back, always returning to G (never below it). Two waves per beat, then three, then four.
watchFor: vibrato that is too wide or too fast to sound musical
vibrato out of time
the pitch dipping below the note

technique.title: Classical Vibrato
technique.pattern: At seventh position or higher (string 1 fret 7 (B)), rock the fingertip along the string, toward and away from the nut, so the pitch moves slightly above and below the note; four waves per beat.
watchFor: side-to-side bending instead of along the string
vibrato on every note without choice

technique.title: Barre Strength Without Strain
technique.pattern: Lay finger 1 flat across all six strings at fret 5. Pick each string from 6 to 1; for any dead string, roll the finger slightly onto its bony side and move it closer to the fret wire. Then press for 2 beats and release (without lifting) for 2 beats, 8 times. Move to fret 3, then fret 1.
watchFor: squeezing with the thumb instead of using arm weight
the barre finger flat on its soft pad
holding the barre for minutes
a sore thumb, hand or forearm: stop and rest, because a clean barre comes from placement and arm weight, not from squeezing harder

technique.title: Fretting-Hand Muting
technique.pattern: Play E5 (022xxx) and let the underside of the fretting fingers touch strings 3-1 so a full strum sounds only strings 6 and 5. Then stop notes by releasing pressure while keeping contact.
watchFor: open strings ringing under power chords
lifting fingers off completely to stop a note

technique.title: Slide (Bottleneck) Intonation
technique.pattern: Wear the slide on finger 3 or 4. Touch the strings lightly directly over the fret wire, not between frets, and mute behind the slide with the fingers trailing it. Targets on string 1 in standard tuning: over fret 12 (E), fret 10 (D), fret 7 (B) and fret 5 (A), each checked against the same fret played normally: string 1 fret 12 (E), string 1 fret 10 (D), string 1 fret 7 (B), string 1 fret 5 (A).
watchFor: pressing the strings down to the frets
slide placed between frets (flat)
noise behind the slide

technique.title: One-Minute Changes: First Chords
technique.pattern: For each pair, Em-G, A-D, D-A7, A-E7, Em-D: strum once per beat and change chord on every beat for 60 seconds; count the clean changes. The app keeps your best count per pair.
watchFor: fingers landing one at a time
stopping the beat to fix a chord
looking for the next shape too late

technique.title: One-Minute Changes: Three-Chord Keys
technique.pattern: Pairs G-C, C-G7, G-D7, D-G, C-Am, Am-E, Am-Dm, E-B7, and D with the open Bm7 (x20202), which stands in for Bm until barre chords: change on every beat for 60 seconds per pair, counting clean changes.
watchFor: ignoring the anchor fingers
tension building over the minute

technique.title: One-Minute Changes: F and Friends
technique.pattern: Pairs Am-Fmaj7, C-F (small F, xx3211), Em-Am, Em-B7, D with the small F#m (xx4222) (finger 3 on string 4, a finger-1 barre on strings 3 to 1), then C-F with the full barre F (133211): change on every beat for 60 seconds per pair.
watchFor: the barre collapsing on the change
arriving late on the F

technique.title: Barre Change Speed
technique.pattern: F (133211) to Bb (x13331) to C (x35553) to Dm (x-5-7-7-6-5), changing every 2 beats, then every beat. Keep finger 1 lightly in contact as it slides between frets.
watchFor: releasing the whole hand between chords
the barre arriving after the strum

technique.title: Triad Inversions on the Top Strings
technique.pattern: Major triads on strings 3, 2 and 1, three shapes for each chord up the neck. C: C (xxx553) root position, C (xxx988) first inversion (E at the bottom), C (x-x-x-12-13-12) second inversion (G at the bottom). F: F (xxx211), F (xxx565), F (x-x-x-10-10-8). G: G (xxx433), G (xxx787), G (x-x-x-12-12-10). Strum strings 3 to 1 only, one chord per beat, naming the top note. Then join C, F, G and C by the nearest shapes, C (xxx553), F (xxx565), G (xxx787), C (xxx988), so the top note climbs G, A, B, C while the hand barely moves.
watchFor: strumming strings 4 to 6 as well
one string of the triad dead under a finger
hunting for each shape instead of hearing the top note move
teaches: voice leading on the top strings

technique.title: Hands in Sync
technique.pattern: The chromatic 1-2-3-4 at a very slow tempo, eighths: each note fretted just before it is picked. Listen for buzz (fretted too late) or gaps (lifted too early). Record and listen back.
watchFor: picking before the finger is down
lifting the previous finger too early

technique.title: Metronome on 2 and 4
technique.pattern: Set the click to sound only on beats 2 and 4 and play any strumming pattern or scale against it, feeling 1 and 3 yourself. Then click on the "and" of each beat only.
watchFor: hearing the click as beat 1
rushing between clicks

technique.title: Odd Meters: 5/4 and 7/8
technique.pattern: 5/4 counted 1 2 3 4 5 and grouped 3+2: accents on beats 1 and 4, strumming Em (022000) on every beat for 8 bars; then grouped 2+3 (accents on 1 and 3). 7/8 counted in eighths and grouped 2+2+3 (accents on 1, 3 and 5) on Am (x02210); then 3+2+2. Count aloud. The click sounds every quarter note in 5/4 and every eighth note in 7/8, so the ladder is that pulse.
watchFor: adding or dropping a beat at the bar line
letting 5/4 turn into a bar of 4/4 and a pause
accents drifting away from the start of each group

technique.title: Natural Harmonics
technique.pattern: Touch the string lightly, directly over the fret wire (do not press it down), pick, then lift the finger. Over fret 12 the harmonic sounds an octave above the open string, over fret 7 an octave and a fifth, over fret 5 two octaves. All six strings at frets 12, 7 and 5.
watchFor: touching between the frets instead of over the wire
pressing the string down
leaving the finger on too long

technique.title: Artificial (Harp) Harmonics
technique.pattern: Fret a note, for example string 5 fret 3 (C); with the picking-hand index finger touch the string 12 frets higher (over fret 15) and pluck with a (or with the thumb). Alternate harmonics and ordinary notes on neighbouring strings for a harp effect.
watchFor: touching at the wrong distance (count exactly 12 frets)
harmonics much quieter than ordinary notes

technique.title: Pinch Harmonics
technique.pattern: Pick a note (string 3 fret 7 (D)) so the edge of the thumb brushes the string just after the pick. Move the picking point toward and away from the neck to find the squeal. Easiest with an overdriven tone.
watchFor: the thumb muting the note completely
searching in one spot only

technique.title: Tapping Triplets
technique.pattern: On string 1: tap string 1 fret 12 (E) with the picking-hand middle finger, pull off to string 1 fret 5 (A) (fretting finger 1), hammer string 1 fret 8 (C) (finger 4). Triplets, steady. Then F (frets 13, 5, 8), G (frets 15, 7, 10) and E (frets 12, 4, 7). Mute the other strings with both hands.
watchFor: the tap too weak to sound
the pull-off not plucking the string
open strings ringing

technique.title: Scales in Every Key, Full Neck
technique.pattern: All 12 major and all 12 melodic minor scales, three notes per string from the lowest root on string 6 or 5 up to the highest playable octave and back, sixteenth notes, in a fixed order around the circle of fifths (C G D A E B F# Db Ab Eb Bb F). Picking players alternate-pick; classical players alternate i-m (and a-m on a second pass). Then the same scales in thirds. Spell every note correctly for its key (F# major has E#, not F).
watchFor: speeding up on easy keys and slowing on hard ones
losing the spelling in sharp and flat keys
tension creeping in above 120
